references.text: The Lord comes down in a cloud to speak with Moses, a recurring motif where God's presence is manifested through the cloud.
The pillar of cloud descends when the Lord speaks with Moses, showing the same theophany of cloud and divine speech.
The Lord comes down in the cloud and stands with Moses, paralleling how God came down in the cloud in Numbers 11:25.
God's promise to take some of the Spirit that is on Moses and give it to the seventy elders, which is fulfilled in verse 25.
Eldad and Medad prophesy in the camp by the same Spirit given to the seventy elders.
The Spirit of the Lord comes upon Saul, and he prophesies, similar to how the Spirit came upon the elders and they prophesied.
God's Spirit comes upon Saul, and he prophesies among the prophets, paralleling the elders who prophesied when the Spirit rested on them.
God's Spirit comes upon Saul's messengers and Saul himself, and they prophesy, demonstrating the Spirit's power to grant prophetic gifts.
Joel's prophecy that God will pour out His Spirit on all flesh and they shall prophesy, an eschatological fulfillment of the gift of the Spirit.
The Holy Spirit is poured out on Pentecost, and the disciples begin to speak in tongues, a New Testament parallel to the outpouring of the Spirit upon the elders.
Peter quotes Joel regarding the outpouring of the Spirit and prophecy, linking Pentecost to the Old Testament tradition of the gift of the Spirit.
